title: Global
summary: Answers reused across scopes. A scoped pack references these instead of copying them.

questions.prompt: Which contrast metric do you name?
questions.summary: The metric is a decision. This pack does not run the formula.

options.label: WCAG 2.2 contrast
options.summary: Relative luminance contrast, as WCAG 2.2 describes it.
options.why: WCAG 2.2 contrast is the ratio of relative luminance between two colors. It matches a target that names WCAG 2.2.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if your target is WCAG 2.2 AA or AAA.
trade_offs: The ratio is not a full reading test

options.label: APCA
options.why: APCA is a different contrast model. It judges lightness with its own formula.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if your team has agreed to use APCA instead of WCAG.
trade_offs: A WCAG target and APCA numbers can disagree
options.formula: APCA lightness contrast, reviewed after values exist.

questions.prompt: Which way do the step numbers run?
questions.summary: Direction includes the range: 50 to 1000, or 100 to 0.

options.label: 50 to 1000
options.summary: A low number is a light color.
options.why: Step names run from 50 to 1000, and a low number is a light color, like the names in Tailwind.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if your team already says 50 for the lightest step.
trade_offs: The numbers are not lightness percents
options.formula: Named stops from 50 through 1000. Lightness falls as the number rises.

options.label: 100 to 0
options.summary: A high number is a light color.
options.why: Step names run from 100 down to 0, and a high number is a light color, like a lightness percent.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if 100 should mean the lightest step.
trade_offs: It goes against the common 50 to 900 habit

questions.prompt: Which CSS unit do space and type use?
questions.summary: The unit is shared by type, space, and radius.

options.label: rem
options.summary: Relative to the root font size.
options.why: Rem follows the reader's font size, so zoom and settings keep the layout in step.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if the product is on the web.
trade_offs: Matching a pixel-exact mock takes more work

options.label: px
options.why: Pixels are fixed. They match a fixed layout and do not follow the reader's font size.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if you need exact pixels on a native screen.

questions.prompt: Do you keep structure and theme apart?
questions.summary: Structure is anatomy, states, and inner spacing. Theme is color, type, radius, and motion.

options.label: Separate
options.summary: Components do not hold theme values.
options.why: Components hold anatomy and states. Theme files hold color, type, radius and motion.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if a new theme must not change the components.
trade_offs: You keep two layers in the repo

options.label: Combined
options.summary: Theme values live in the components.
options.why: Theme values live in the component files, so one folder holds the whole look.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if you have one brand and want fewer files.
trade_offs: A second brand means editing components
